sources.entry: Screenpipe - Captures screen text and audio transcripts locally, making computer history searchable for people and AI assistants through MCP and a local API. #freemium

summary.name: Screenpipe
summary.one_liner: Screenpipe is a tool that records your screen text and audio locally so you and AI assistants can search your computer history and discover repeated workflows.
use_cases: Searching past screen content or conversations
Mapping repeated workflows to find automation opportunities
Giving AI agents context about your work history
Drafting meeting summaries and follow-ups from captured audio
Reviewing how invoices or other processes were handled
summary.what_it_does: Screenpipe captures screen activity (accessibility data, screen frames with OCR fallback) and audio transcripts, storing them in a local database. You can scrub back through your day to find a specific screen, document, or conversation. It exposes a local REST API and an MCP server so AI agents can query your history. The page describes a workflow discovery view that shows recurring steps across apps and flags exceptions, using sample data. Controls let you exclude apps, windows, and URLs and redact sensitive fields on the device.
notable: Raw history stays local by default, with a local database, REST API, and MCP server
Captures accessibility data, OCR-fallback screen frames, and audio transcripts
Workflow discovery that maps recurring steps and exceptions across apps
Enterprise workspace for device management, policies, and audit trails
caveats: Enterprise deployment features (device management, identity, policies, audit trails) are described without pricing details
Workflow examples on the page use sample data
